newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief announces staff, budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief announces staff, budget cuts.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan called on Monday for staff and budget cuts and the merging of some U.N. departments under his control as the first step in his promised programme to reform the United Nations.
Annan, in a statement to a U.N. committee, revealed his so-called "track one" initiatives which could be enacted immediately. They are to be followed up by another, fuller report in July.
Annan announced a reduction of 1,000 staff posts for the secretariat or core U.N. staff which has about 9,000 employees based primarily in New York, Geneva and Nairobi.

He also announced $123 million in budget cuts for 1998-1999. The current budget is about $1 billion annually. He said he would consolidate departments dealing with economic and social issues and reduce documentation.

Annan said 38 percent of the organisation's resources were devoted to administration. He said he was committed to reducing this by a third and channelling the resources to economic and social programmes for the developing world.

The secretary-general took office on Jan. 1 after the United States vetoed his predecessor, Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt, for allegedly not doing enough to reform the world body. The conservative U.S. Congress has vowed not to pay the $1 billion Washington owes the United Nations until it is satisfied with Annan's reform programme.
